title: 01 Linear equations and inequalities: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 01 Linear equations and inequalities: Visual Guide

1. Three Possible Fates | four draggable coefficients in Ax + B = Cx + D reduced live to ax = b, beside the rank trichotomy for a linear system, with presets for the quiz equations | one solution is the generic case and needs a nonzero coefficient; 0 = 0 means infinitely many and a false statement like 5 = -1 means no solution, which is not the same as x = 0

2. Clear The Clutter | three costumes of one equation - k(x-2)=9, x/d+2=5 and 0.5x+c=4.5 - each solved step by step from a live slider, with the distribute-to-the-first-term-only error computed alongside | distribute to every term and multiply BOTH sides by the LCD or by a power of ten; the cleaning move is what turns a cluttered equation back into ax = b

3. The Taxi Meter | a cost line with draggable starting amount b and per-mile rate m, an evaluation point, a measured rise-over-run readout and a swap button drawing the b·x + m distractor | m is the rate of change and b is the starting amount at x = 0, so C = 2m + 4 and C = 4m + 2 are different businesses and the units check tells them apart

4. Distance From A Point | a number line where dragging the centre c and the distance d in |x - c| = d marks the solutions c - d and c + d, collapsing to one at d = 0 and to none when d is negative | absolute value is nonnegative distance, so the equation splits into two branches and answers come in symmetric pairs c ± d - reporting only the positive branch is the standard miss

5. And Versus Or | a multi-step chain a·x - 4 ≥ 8 whose sign flips live as the coefficient crosses zero, plus a shaded number line switching between intersection and union with interval notation | dividing by a negative reverses the inequality and nothing else does; "and" is an intersection that can be empty while "or" is a union of two intervals that can cover all of R
